title: The Fragile Foundation of Trust
text:
Trust is an abstract noun that denotes a firm belief in the reliability of another person or institution. Sociologists contend that trust is the foundation of cooperation, since people rarely engage in long-term exchanges without some expectation of fairness. Nevertheless, trust is fragile and can erode quickly after a single betrayal. Its absence often leads to elaborate contracts and surveillance, which are costly to maintain.

Recent studies of urban neighbourhoods suggest that trust is shaped less by individual character than by everyday encounters. Residents who meet regularly in shared spaces tend to develop a modest but durable confidence in one another. Accordingly, policymakers increasingly invest in public libraries and community gardens. Such initiatives indicate that trust, though intangible, can be deliberately cultivated.

questions.text: According to paragraph one, what does trust denote?
options: A firm belief in the reliability of another person or institution

questions.text: According to paragraph two, where do residents develop confidence in one another?
options: In shared spaces where they meet regularly

questions.text: What can be inferred about societies in which trust is absent?
options: They rely more heavily on contracts and surveillance
They never engage in any cooperation
They have no need for public institutions
They value trust more than fairness

questions.text: What does the author imply about the role of policymakers?
options: They can deliberately build trust through public investment
They have no influence on everyday encounters
They should rely solely on individual character

vocabulary.definition: the quality of being trustworthy and consistent
the act of working together towards a shared goal
able to last for a long time without becoming weak

paragraph_translations: Güven, başka bir kişinin ya da kurumun güvenilirliğine duyulan sağlam inancı belirten soyut bir isimdir. Sosyologlar güvenin iş birliğinin temelini oluşturduğunu savunur, çünkü insanlar adalete dair bir beklenti olmadan uzun vadeli alışverişlere nadiren girer. Yine de güven kırılgandır ve tek bir ihanetten sonra hızla aşınabilir. Güvenin yokluğu çoğu zaman karmaşık sözleşmelere ve gözetime yol açar; bunların sürdürülmesi ise maliyetlidir.

Kentsel mahallelere yönelik son araştırmalar, güvenin bireysel karakterden çok gündelik karşılaşmalarla şekillendiğini göstermektedir. Ortak alanlarda düzenli olarak buluşan sakinler birbirlerine mütevazı ama dayanıklı bir güven geliştirme eğilimindedir. Buna göre politika yapıcılar giderek halk kütüphanelerine ve toplumsal bahçelere yatırım yapmaktadır. Bu tür girişimler, güvenin somut olmasa da bilinçli olarak geliştirilebileceğini ortaya koymaktadır.
